title: Black Unemployment at 6.6% and the Shrinking Federal Ladder | Across the Water, Ep. 8
lede: The Black unemployment rate fell to 6.6% in October, but the number of employed Black workers fell too. Behind the headline sits a longer story: the federal workforce, long a path into the Black middle class, shrank 12% between September 2024 and January 2026. This episode explains the October jobs report, why federal jobs mattered, who left, how each side reads the cuts and where the economy is hiring now.
keyPoints: Black unemployment was 6.6% in October 2026, down from 7.0%; white 3.7%, overall 4.1%. Employed Black workers fell by 56,000 (BLS; Joint Center).
The Black rate was 6.2% in January 2025 and peaked at 8.2% in November 2025 (BLS via FRED).
The federal civilian workforce fell from 2,313,216 (Sept 2024) to 2,035,344 (Jan 2026), down 12% (Partnership for Public Service, OPM data).

Black Americans were 18.5% of the federal civil service in 2024, vs about 12% of civilian employment (Pew via Marketplace); a Washington Post analysis of Census survey estimates found Black federal employment down about 20% in Jan–Sep 2026 vs 2024.
October hiring was led by professional and business services (+70,000) and health care (+42,000) (BLS).
